abstract: Protein domain and protein family models comprising the Conserved Domain Database (CDD) are widely used at the National Center of Biotechnology Information to inform protein textual and graphical summary pages with the location of domain footprints, domain architecture, and derived functional sites, and to name proteins by domain architecture when names cannot be obtained from higher-ranked, more specific sources. CDD continues to add novel protein domain models, constructed as multiple sequence alignments, to its collection via import of external data sources and an in-house curation effort. CDD has been available publicly for ~25 years and continues to update a substantial archive of pre-computed annotation for rapid dissemination of information, provide live database search services that can support moderate numbers of requests, and downloadable data and software to run data analyses locally. CDD can be accessed at https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Structure/cdd/cdd.shtml.
